speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness; can you tell me if these symptoms started all at once or have they been getting worse over time?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: The double vision triggered by looking up or down, combined with fatigue that worsens with activity and improves with rest, strongly suggests a neuromuscular issue like Myasthenia Gravis. REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies. REQUEST TEST: Repetitive_Nerve_Stimulation.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The presence of elevated acetylcholine receptor antibodies and decreased muscle response on repetitive nerve stimulation confirm the diagnosis suggested by your symptoms of fluctuating weakness and diplopia.
